text: Small learned models and independently checked biological ODEs Study a Poisson PINN, periodic-heat FNO and enzyme, predator–prey and SEIR systems under fixed budgets. Original learning and approximation goals remain separate from reproduction checks. These additional validation supplements are managed separately from the common 22-example registry. Receipts cover independent ZIP extraction, tests and every fixed input within each group. Changes of settings, methods or step sizes do not add independent physical problems. Routine supplement CI runs the supplement groups listed in the public registry with NumPy,SciPy and pytest. It checks versions,inputs and execution records for stored independent references and distinguishes their reuse from new reference computations. The existing common22-case suite,including quantum convergence,remains manual on explicit need; released artifacts,criteria and history are preserved. Download and execute the supplement Run inside atlas-small-models-2026-11-25 from the ZIP. This command executes all 5 fixed cases in the supplement. The bundled results/ contains stored outputs. Rerun into a new output/ directory, and choose another fresh directory for subsequent runs. python -m pip install -r requirements.txt python -m pytest -q python run.py --input inputs.json --output output Matplotlib is optional for redrawing saved figures; ordinary scientific execution does not require it. Poisson PINN: independent grid error Compare a 49-parameter PINN for three fixed seeds with analytic and finite-difference solutions. Methods, equations, figures and references Assumptions, units and boundaries Solve dimensionless −uₓₓ=π² sin(πx) on [0,1] with zero Dirichlet data. Use sixteen hidden units, 49 real parameters, seeds 8401–8403, 64 training points and 257 separate evaluation points. Editorial clarification This fixed-budget study covers one smooth Poisson problem and three seeds. A small training loss does not establish independent-point accuracy or general PINN training success. Unmet goals remain visible. Adopted numerical method Train a hard-boundary tanh ansatz with trust-region reflective least squares and an analytic parameter Jacobian. Retain every returned model under the fixed budget. Tiny FNO on held-out heat problems Evaluate the same learned weights on 32/64-point grids, held-out functions and separate OOD inputs. Methods, equations, figures and references Assumptions, units and boundaries Use periodic heat flow uₜ=νuₓₓ on [0,2π) to T=0.25. Split 46 whole problems into 24 training, 6 validation, 8 held-out ID, 4 viscosity-OOD and 4 spectrum-OOD problems. Use two fixed seeds and 93 real parameters. Editorial clarification This comparison concerns a fixed tiny discrete operator, without arbitrary-resolution, distributional or OOD guarantees. The N=64-to-32 discrepancy includes nonlinear aliasing and is not a continuum discretization error. Optimizer convergence is distinct from normal budget termination. The old heat primary remains. This [0,2pi) whole-problem family, diffusivities and final time are separate fixed inputs. Adopted numerical method Lift (u₀,ν) to width two and apply two blocks containing a local linear map, real DC and complex Fourier modes 1–4, then tanh. Train with a fixed L-BFGS-B budget and evaluate the same weights at N=32 and 64. Nonlinear terms are evaluated on each native grid without dealiasing. ut=νuxx,x∈[0,2π),u(x+2π,t)=u(x,t),T=14ut​=νuxx​,x∈[0,2π),u(x+2π,t)=u(x,t),T=41​ u^k(T)=e−νk2Tu^k(0)uk​(T)=e−νk2Tuk​(0) vℓ+1=tanh⁡ ⁣(Wℓvℓ+bℓ+FN−1(RℓFNvℓ)),ℓ=0,1vℓ+1=tanh(Wℓ​vℓ+bℓ​+FN−1​(Rℓ​FN​vℓ)),ℓ=0,1 relative error=RMS⁡(uθ−uref)RMS⁡(uref)only if RMS⁡(uref)>10−12relative error=RMS(uref​)RMS(uθ​−uref​)​only if RMS(uref​)>10−12 References and measured quantities Qualify all 93 real loss-gradient coordinates at two fixed finite-difference widths and compare Fourier blocks with direct DFT sums. PDF header/edition only; not full paper or appendix audit. Enzyme conservation and QSSA Separate the initial layer, integration error and QSSA modeling error in a four-state enzyme mechanism. Methods, equations, figures and references Assumptions, units and boundaries Use the closed dimensionless reaction E+S⇌C→E+P with k₁=10, k₋₁=k₂=1, S₀=1, C₀=P₀=0 and E₀=0.01 or 0.002. Then Kₘ=0.2, ε=E₀/(Kₘ+S₀)=1/120 or 1/600, and θ=E₀t ranges from 0 to 0.5. Editorial clarification These two small-ε fixed-rate examples are educational. ε is a scale ratio, not itself a certified QSSA error bound. The θ≥0.02 window is not a proof that the initial layer has ended, and the calculation is not an in-vivo prediction. Time, concentrations and populations do not define a spatial dimension. The rates are educational, not disease or experimental predictions. Adopted numerical method Integrate all four states with SDIRK2 step doubling, using the same weighted L∞ residual for Newton convergence and Armijo backtracking. Evolve the reduced Michaelis–Menten equation separately with RK4 in θ, keeping integration error distinct from model-reduction error. Lotka–Volterra invariant and positivity Compare a positive orbit against an independently integrated log-coordinate reference. Methods, equations, figures and references Assumptions, units and boundaries Use the dimensionless predator–prey equations x′=x(1−y), y′=y(x−1), initial state (1.2,0.8) and 0≤t≤20. Evaluate H=x−log x+y−log y only in the positive quadrant. Editorial clarification This is a finite-time comparison for one initial state. The continuum closed orbit is not an attracting limit cycle. RK4 is not claimed to preserve H exactly, maintain positivity at arbitrary steps or guarantee long-time geometric fidelity. Time, concentrations and populations do not define a spatial dimension. The rates are educational, not disease or experimental predictions. Adopted numerical method Integrate physical populations with classical RK4 at 400, 800 and 1600 fixed steps. Methods, equations, figures and references Assumptions, units and boundaries Use a closed population S+E+I+R=1 with β=0.6, σ=0.3 and γ=0.2. For η=10⁻⁴ or 5×10⁻⁵, start from (1−2η,η,η,0) and evolve to t=20. There are no births, deaths or external inflows. Editorial clarification These fixed-coefficient calculations compare two small initial infection levels. The early linearization is not an exact solution through t=20, and a single dominant mode does not replace the two-mode solution. No epidemic forecast, statistical coverage or arbitrary-population guarantee is claimed. Time, concentrations and populations do not define a spatial dimension. The rates are educational, not disease or experimental predictions. Adopted numerical method Evolve all four physical states with RK4 at 400, 800 and 1600 fixed steps. Independently compute the nonlinear reference with scaled-deviation Radau/BDF and the early E/I linearization with both modes of the full 2×2 matrix exponential.
